rule.description: A method of a package-local struct type whose body makes at least 3 field selections into one other package-local struct type, and at least as many selections into that owner as into its own receiver, is carrying that owner's data interest; the behavior belongs with the data.

checks.description: Detect methods that page through another struct's fields by hand instead of asking that owner to interpret its own data.
checks.detected_relation: method -> field selections of another package-local struct type (count >= 3 and count >= selections on its own receiver, including selections reached through a stored handle or a fetched local)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Feature envy: the method works another owner's data harder than (or equally as hard as) its own, so every change to the owner's representation reaches across a type boundary while the owner learns nothing about how its data is used.

matches.evidence: The presentation method fetches the run's settings through the handle it holds and re-decides every reporting mode itself: s.list, s.write and s.doDiff in the changed-file branch and again in the no-mode branch (6 selections of session state vs 3 selections of its own report fields).

The same method interprets the work record field by field: it compares fh.data with fh.rendered to decide whether formatting changed, prints fh.display for the listing mode, overwrites the file at fh.display with fh.rendered for write-back, and writes fh.rendered to the output stream when no mode was chosen (6 selections of sourceFile field state).

The diff presentation is assembled entirely from record fields: diff(fh.data, fh.rendered), the fh.display name repeated in gofmt's 'diff %s gofmt/%s' header, and one selection of the report's own out stream (4 selections of sourceFile field state vs 1 of its own).

The stdin traversal method re-implements run decisions: it copies s.opts, re-derives fragment mode from s.stdin for itself, and re-checks s.list, s.write and s.doDiff to write formatted text directly (5 selections of session state vs 2 selections of its own walker fields).

The same method owns nothing of the record it mutates: it fills fh.data from standard input, hands fh.display and fh.data to the formatter, stores the result in fh.rendered and writes fh.rendered itself in the no-mode branch (5 selections of sourceFile field state vs 2 of its own walker fields).

The named-file traversal method computes the rendered text by handing the record's own fh.display and fh.data to the formatter and stuffing the result back into fh.rendered (3 selections of sourceFile field state vs 0 of its own walker fields).

excluded.what: report.noteProblem bumps one foreign field (the run's failure tally) and writes one own stream; below the rule's floor of 3, and the field is updated, never interpreted.
walker.paths, walker.visitFile and walker.processFile pass the session and the record around as whole objects and read no fields of them; routing is collaboration, not data interest.
session.optionsFor and session.failed read their own receiver's state where it lives; clean counterexamples inside the injected state.

gofmtMain, diff and isGoFile are plain functions (outside a method-level rule about receivers); imports.Options and other stdlib or golang.org/x/tools types are not declared in this package, so behavior cannot be re-homed toward them in this repository.
